title: Adam Smith and the Pin Factory: the Economics of Specialization (1776)
explainer: In The Wealth of Nations, Adam Smith opens with the famous example of a pin factory: a single worker making pins alone can produce only a handful a day, but ten workers each specializing in one of eighteen distinct steps can produce thousands. Smith used this to argue that dividing labor into focused specialties, rather than each person doing everything, is what drives large gains in skill and output. It is a useful lens for choosing a specialization deliberately: depth in one area compounds in a way that stretching thin across everything usually doesn't.
